name: Threshold scatter
reader_question: Which items fall beyond a stated reference value on one or both measures?
relationship: Association between two measures read against one or two stated reference thresholds that divide the plane into quadrants.
use_when: A source or analyst states a threshold on at least one measure and the reader needs to see who is beyond it
Quadrant membership is the message and exact values are secondary
avoid_when: No stated threshold exists; drawing one invents a criterion — use scatter
A third measure must also be encoded — use bubble

data_contract.notes: Explicit axis range containing every point and every threshold
One or two reference values; breach states which side counts as beyond
Unique items; points beyond every supplied threshold are drawn in the accent

units: Each axis states its own unit; thresholds are expressed in the unit of their axis.

editable: Native scatter chart with embedded workbook (Edit Data)
not_data_bound: Threshold lines, quadrant captions and point labels are positioned shapes and text computed from the fixture; they do not move if chart data or axis range is edited
The accent/neutral split is two series computed from the thresholds at build time

table_alternative: A table of items with a flag column stating which thresholds each item breaches.
limitations: Thresholds must be stated or sourced; an analyst-chosen cut-off is a presentation choice and is labelled as such
Items near a threshold look categorically different from items just across it

excluded_alternatives.reason: Fills would compete with the single accent and imply four classes of equal standing
Collapsing two measures into one index would hide the thresholds' separate meaning
